extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO Director when a practitioner has resigned or been disciplined by a state court, including respondent's opportunity to contest, duties during exclusion, and publication/notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., exclusion from practice before the Office) where a practitioner has been disciplined by a state court, including where the practitioner's resignation in lieu of disciplinary proceeding has been accepted by that court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order was based on the Texas Supreme Court's acceptance of Respondent's Motion of Acceptance of Resignation and striking his name from the roll of attorneys. The Director determined, after the Notice and Order and expiration of the response period, that exclusion of Respondent from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's right and burden to contest under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks to contest imposition of exclusion under § 11.24(d), the respondent must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that identical discipline would be unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must address any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response may result in the Director determining there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation in lieu of disciplinary proceeding as basis for exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's resignation in lieu of disciplinary proceeding accepted by a state court (resulting in removal from the roll of attorneys) is a ground for imposing reciprocal exclusion under § 11.24(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically cites the practitioner's consent to have his name stricken while a disciplinary proceeding was pending and his resignation acknowledging inability to contest charges as the basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of professional misconduct supporting state action
rubrics_metrics.description: The state disciplinary charges alleged professional misconduct including: neglecting legal matters entrusted to the lawyer; failing to keep clients reasonably informed; failing to promptly deliver funds and other property clients are entitled to receive; failing to withdraw when continued representation will result in violation of the disciplinary rules; failing to comply with obligations on termination of representation; and failing to respond to lawful requests of a disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These misconduct types were the factual predicates for the state court acceptance of resignation and are the kinds of conduct that can support reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effect of exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion means the respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the exclusion begins on the effective date (e.g., January 22, 2010 in this case) and is imposed pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client business (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for a short period (here, beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after) to wind up all client business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this limited recognition the respondent is directed to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40 and must not accept any new clients with business before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to withdraw from pending proceedings (37 C.F.R. § 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: While winding up client matters under the limited recognition period, respondent is directed to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires following the withdrawal procedures set out in § 10.40 (notification, steps to protect client interests, etc.). The Final Order expressly directs withdrawal during the limited recognition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express restriction on practice to allow orderly wind-up and protect client interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (OED Director responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order, publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette, post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room, and give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary agencies and courts where the practitioner is admitted, and to the public, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.59 and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion should identify the practitioner, registration number, the basis for exclusion, effective date, and statutory/regulatory authority; decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room URL. The Director's notice fulfills transparency and inter-jurisdictional communication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with obligations while excluded (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded from practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not restate § 11.58, it imposes the obligation to follow whatever duties and restrictions that section prescribes during the period of exclusion (e.g., restrictions on representing others before the Office, use of title, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires full compliance with the reinstatement procedures and standards set out in § 11.60 as the condition for any restoration of practice privileges before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action and publication are taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authorities, here cited as 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These authorities provide the legal basis for issuing reciprocal discipline, publishing notices, and communicating with other jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification of mailing (37 C.F.R. § 11.11 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service showing the order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service to the respondent and certification of that service is required for disciplinary orders and is documented in the record.
